title: Genesis Mission Awardee Hopes to Challenge ASML with X-Ray Lithography
snippet: When it comes to bottlenecks in the semiconductor supply chain, there is a massive one right at the top: ASML. The Dutch manufacturer is a functional monopoly, owning 100% of the market for the extreme ultraviolet (EUV)…
contentText: When it comes to bottlenecks in the semiconductor supply chain, there is a massive one right at the top: ASML. The Dutch manufacturer is a functional monopoly, owning 100% of the market for the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines required to manufacture advanced semiconductors. One startup that hopes to challenge that monopoly one day is Inversion Semiconductor, which recently won a Genesis Mission award from the Department of Energy to study the use of AI in chipmaking. ASML owns a monopoly on EUV lithography machines for one very good reason: The machines are extremely difficult to build. ASML has decades of hands-on experience in building these unfathomably complex lithography machines, which cost up to $400 million apiece and have more than 100,000 parts. ASML acts more lik…

title: Compute Clusters Break Out Of National Labs To Scale AI
snippet: For compute-intensive applications, clusters of nodes that act as a single computer offer a way to scale performance and provide a workaround for organizations that lack access to leading-edge AI chips. The post Compute…
contentText: Key Takeaways: A cluster comprises a group of interconnected servers (aka nodes) across multiple racks, connected via Ethernet and increasingly via optical links, and is ideal for workloads that are so large and require so much compute that a single rack of servers cannot do the job. Design challenges include network congestion, latency and stragglers, power delivery, thermal limits, software scheduling, performance and scalability, and power and energy. Clusters are already deployed in national labs for use cases such as global weather simulations, but widespread AI is pushing the solution into manufacturing, drug discovery, financial risk modeling, EDA, autonomous vehicles, and more. contentText: For many years — well before AI compute’s “big bang” in late 2022 — the data center industry has been preoccupied with the notion of designing denser racks to improve overall infrastructure economics. It has also regularly advocated for the use of direct liquid cooling (DLC). Indeed, the underlying megatrend is clearly toward increased density, pushed on by the gradual rise in power of IT silicon components. This is compounded by a trend toward richer server configurations and the economic drive to increase system utilization — despite real-world data on the latter being sparse. title: Trump administration admits grants for clean energy were canceled based on politics
snippet: The Trump administration admitted in court that it canceled $7.6 billion in clean energy grants for 16 states that voted for Kamala Harris in 2024, citing political identity as the reason.
contentText: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration has acknowledged in court documents that it canceled $7.6 billion in grants for hundreds of clean energy projects “based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state” — in this case, 16 states that voted for Democrat Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. The statement contradicts repeated assertions by Energy Secretary Chris Wright and other officials that the projects were canceled because they did not adequately advance the nation’s energy needs or had other problems that made them a poor investment of taxpayer dollars. title: Google just redesigned the search box for the first time in 25 years — here’s why it matters more than you think.
snippet: For a quarter century, the Google search box has been one of the most recognizable interfaces in computing: a thin white rectangle, a blinking cursor, a few typed words, and a list of blue links. On Tuesday, Google will…
contentText: For a quarter century, the Google search box has been one of the most recognizable interfaces in computing: a thin white rectangle, a blinking cursor, a few typed words, and a list of blue links. On Tuesday, Google will formally retire that paradigm. At its annual I/O developer conference , Google announced a sweeping redesign of the search box itself — the literal text field where billions of queries begin every day — transforming it from a simple keyword input into a dynamic, AI-driven conversation starter that can accept text, images, PDFs, videos, and even open Chrome tabs as inputs.
